description: A single-panel figure consisting of one chemical-composition table rendered as an image (no other panels, axes, micrographs or curves). The table is headed "Steels" with a spanning column header "Chemical composition, wt.%" and twelve elemental columns: C, Si, Mn, P, S, Al, Mo, Ni, Cr, Ti, Nb and Fe. Four alloy rows are listed by grade name: 3Cr, 2Ni, 2Ni3Cr and 2Ni5Cr. Carbon ranges from 1.23 wt.% (2Ni) to 1.41 wt.% (2Ni3Cr); Mn 20.1–21.0 wt.%; Al 8.21–9.35 wt.%; Si 0.35–0.37 wt.%; Mo 0.51–0.57 wt.%; P and S are at impurity levels (P 0.009–0.011, S 0.001–0.002 wt.%); Ti is 0.01 wt.% and Nb 0.03 wt.% in every row; Fe is given as "Bal." throughout. The deliberate Ni/Cr variation is directly readable: 3Cr has 0.18 Ni with 2.88 Cr, 2Ni has 2.05 Ni with 0.05 Cr, 2Ni3Cr has 2.11 Ni with 2.89 Cr, and 2Ni5Cr has 2.08 Ni with 4.90 Cr. The table documents the measured bulk compositions of the four Fe–20Mn–9Al-1.5C-xNi-yCr steels, confirming the intended Ni and Cr alloying levels were realised.

subfigures.description: A chemical-composition table (wt.%) for four steels labelled 3Cr, 2Ni, 2Ni3Cr and 2Ni5Cr, with columns C, Si, Mn, P, S, Al, Mo, Ni, Cr, Ti, Nb and Fe; Fe is reported as 'Bal.' in all rows.

observations.observation: The figure is a single table headed 'Steels' with a spanning header 'Chemical composition, wt.%' and elemental columns C, Si, Mn, P, S, Al, Mo, Ni, Cr, Ti, Nb and Fe.
Four steel rows are tabulated by grade name: 3Cr, 2Ni, 2Ni3Cr and 2Ni5Cr.
Across all four steels Mn lies between 20.1 and 21.0 wt.% and Al between 8.21 and 9.35 wt.%, consistent with a Fe–20Mn–9Al base composition.
Ti (0.01 wt.%) and Nb (0.03 wt.%) are identical in every row, and Fe is reported as 'Bal.' in every row.
Ni and Cr vary systematically between rows: 0.18 Ni/2.88 Cr (3Cr), 2.05 Ni/0.05 Cr (2Ni), 2.11 Ni/2.89 Cr (2Ni3Cr) and 2.08 Ni/4.90 Cr (2Ni5Cr) in wt.%.
The caption states the table gives measured chemical compositions of the four Fe–20Mn–9Al-1.5C-xNi-yCr (x = 0, 2 wt%, y = 0, 3, 5 wt%) steels.
The caption identifies the table as measured (analysed) rather than nominal composition, so the printed values are experimental chemical analyses.
